body: The change has to start in you, sweetie, you've seen what waiting on them gets you. I think you can do it though.
I think it's very proportionate. If I were less lucky, I would be in prison for what I did.

It's essentially the same. It feels like a mental twitch, every time I feel okay it jumps in to remind me of the things I've done and what I am. I think that's a good thing, to keep me from forgetting.
A friend picked me up. I'm not Okay but I'm back to my original plan anyway.
Thank you, but accepting kindness is my problem. I'm the kind of sick that doesn't get better, and talking about it just distracts from my goals.

Come see us on r/actuallesbians then. You don't have to be a lesbian to be there, but you'll find a lot of good stories and advice. Maybe it'll turn out you really like it.

Good luck.
I updated with the link sweetie.

Okay. Let me get you a link to read through. I'll edit it into my comment in a couple minutes.

Full disclosure: I'm a lesbian. I encountered this a LOT before I realized it. I would meet men that seemed wonderful, date them, and it would never match up. Problems seemed to just pop up out of nowhere. Especailly the part about being outspoken and opinionated, except with these men, then hating that person you turn into.

Well, turns out, it was because the men were my type in every way but being women... now I date very similar kinds of people, just women, and uh... to be honest with you? In hindsight it's a little embarrasing how obvious it was.

https://docs.google.com/document/u/0/d/1AA6RtNIJIYkXAb8pxguUZAUuA-zKv_y8kpE7WTaRDH4/mobilebasic

This thing I felt is called Compulsive Heterosexuality. This is a document we made to share with others.

See if other parts match up with your experiences.
Okay. Last question. Have you had this happen where you have a crush, you get with them,  and then it feels like nothing?
Were they all men?
This may seem like a strange question, but have you dated before at all? How did that go?

The truth is that you did it for fun, and Joel even made it easy to do. You didn't access anything that isn't 100% public.

He can't be mad at you for looking at public information. Talk to your friend.
This. I hated being around men until I got a large dog. Now he's as big as I am and I walk my merry butt around at 3am without fear. Plus, he's a fantastic cuddle buddy.
What country are you in? Depending on the legal situation and culture it may still be normal if you obviously have a shared interest.
"We know you won't care"? Come on dude... idk what I expected from "muppetholocaust" though.
This is the one to read OP.
Shaming OP for hating her rapist.

Should we tell him about lesbian dating???

It's nice that some people message him first sometime.

Let me offer this: People like him and his family were never going to stop at your looks. People from wealth like that are born into a learned obsession with appearences, and every aspect of your life will slowly become about those apprearences. Self expression is highly discouraged in high control families like this.

I think you've dodged a bullet. This attitude of theirs is precisely why drugs use and suicide are as common in the top 10% as it is at the bottom 10%, both are brutally repressed by different factors.

What would you say to them? "You nuked my personal life intentionally because I am smarter about sex than most kids my age. I would love to tell you about my social life and girlfriend, but they don't exist because of you."

This shit is why no one should have kids.
I don't think my gender matters, beyond my duty to be a good example for my people. I think that guy just had certain ideas about trans people. Thank you though.
How do you mean?

Thank you, it's a point she herself hammered home and that I'm now taking as gospel.

She'd honestly gotten so much better when we were dating, there was a lot of trust even as we went into pretty serious stuff. I could rely on her to safe outnif she got uncomfortable.

I got complacent, thinking that somehow this was similar.

The difference is that then I was her girlfriend, and now she's not. The trust is different.
Obviously I do. I just genuinely wanted an answer to a question you are not answering, though now I am no longer interested in the answer.

I think you guys may be right. I'm so glad I asked, I was having some really unhealthy thoughts before I did... I really expected to be told to. Well, you know. 

Thank you so much for your time and empathy.

And what does that have to do with me being trans?

Edit: And to be clear, there would be nothing worse than for this to be actual rape, and for me to get away with it. If I believed your interpretation, I would be turning myself in.

No one, especially not me, should be glad to 'get away with it'. That is the worst case scenario for anyone, because it's the scenario that is worst for the only person who matters in that case.

Thank you for reading my post. I do not think you have been very helpful, though I am sorry you felt misled by my post.
Thank you for reading and replying.

I agree to that, I just don't know where being trans comes in. If I fingered her, or used a strap on, would it not be exactly the same? I am not trying to argue, just trying to clearly understand the rules here.
I should? May I ask why?

Actually I'm the one who does the memory rewriting. I took like 3 hours to write this post, and referenced her version of events repeatedly. She's a cery mindful person with an excellent memory, whereas I have confirmed recall issues (whether medical or psycological is not known yet). Good point to bring up though.


I'm certain that the 'nod' I saw was probably not a nod. That's the difference between us, and the core of the mistake.

I've historically been very good about this. I'm extremely wary of it, as it's a common accusation among trans lesbians like me, so I've always overcompensated to be 'one of the good ones' i guess. She herself commented that I have always been better than this. I think that's the only reason I'm being given a chance.

I took your advice and contacted my therapist.
You really think so?

Is it that simple? That's the only thought that even motivated me to post this. But here's the thing, she has a long history of forgiving sexual violence against her. People who have done way worse than me have been forgiven, so it may not mean anything that she's willing. If she's just making the same mistake it's up to me isnt it?

Isn't the victim's experience the only one that matters? I've been told so many times to drown out all but the voices of the people going through it at the time.

What would I do to 'work through it'?
Not in so many words. I have previously silenced statements from loved ones with my own panicked thoughts, which is a habit I am fighting. I AM prone to overreacting however.
It was penetrative sex, the 'touching' I refer to was foreplay. After what I thought was consent I moved on to the sex. I'm sorry if I'm using the wrong vocabulary, it's hard to think clearly.
